body: Every automation feature on this model exists to answer one question: can a robot, not a person, run this reliably.

The lid answers it first, opening and closing under software control with a wider opening than standard, so a robotic arm has the clearance it needs. The rotor answers it next, stopping at indexed, fixed positions so loading and unloading happen at a predictable spot every time, not wherever the rotor happened to stop spinning. The sample holders were redesigned around a secure robotic grip specifically. And the RS232 command set ties it together, giving automation software control over the complete machine, not just individual settings.

faqs.question: What makes the miVac 2 different from other vacuum concentrators?
faqs.answer: It combines a modular three-model system with a SpeedTrap condenser capable of freeze-drying very low volumes of water at -50°C, and aluminum JetRotors stated to run up to 40% faster than comparable machines.

faqs.question: What's the difference between the DNA, Duo, and Quattro models?
faqs.answer: DNA removes trace water and volatile solvents that interfere with PCR and NGS, Duo is a general-purpose workhorse compatible with varied sample formats, and Quattro doubles Duo's capacity for high-throughput evaporation.

faqs.question: How do I choose between the three miVac 2 models?
faqs.answer: Match your primary workflow: choose DNA for molecular biology prep ahead of PCR or NGS, Duo for general concentration across mixed sample formats, or Quattro when you need double the throughput.

faqs.question: How do I set up freeze-drying on the miVac 2?
faqs.answer: Confirm the freeze-drying option is included in your configuration, since it's available as an add-on rather than standard, then use the SpeedTrap condenser's -50°C capability for very low-volume water removal.

faqs.question: What types of solvents can the miVac 2 handle?
faqs.answer: Water and a wide range of organic solvents; a complete compatibility list is available directly from Inkarp for your specific application.

faqs.question: Can the miVac 2 replace a freeze dryer?
faqs.answer: It freeze-dries very low volumes of water via the SpeedTrap condenser, which covers specific low-volume needs; confirm with Inkarp whether it fits your workflow or whether a dedicated freeze dryer is still needed.

faqs.question: What sample formats does the miVac 2 support?
faqs.answer: Microcentrifuge tubes, conical or other plastic tubes, glass vials, and shallow- or deep-well microplates, with the Duo model specifically built for this range.

faqs.question: What type of vacuum pump does the miVac 2 use?
faqs.answer: This is confirmed directly by Inkarp based on your specific model and configuration.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the miVac 2 and the EZ-2 4.0 Bionic?
faqs.answer: The miVac 2 offers three purpose-built models and freeze-drying capability, while the Bionic is built specifically around robotic automation with an RS232 command set and indexed rotor; they solve different problems within the same category.

sections.title: SpeedTrap Condenser and Freeze-Drying Capability
sections.tabSummary: What -50°C freeze-drying actually enables
body: Removing trace water from a sample usually means switching to a separate freeze dryer. The SpeedTrap condenser is built to avoid that step for low-volume work.

Reaching an ultimate low temperature of -50°C, it freeze-dries very low volumes of water directly within the same evaporation workflow. That matters most for the DNA model's core job, clearing the trace water and volatile solvents that would otherwise interfere with PCR and NGS, but it's a capability available across the line where freeze-drying is selected as an option.

sections.title: Sample Protection: Dri-Pure and eXalt Technology
sections.tabSummary: What anti-bumping and controlled crystallization actually protect
body: Two named technologies handle two different risks during evaporation: violent bumping that can damage or lose a sample, and uncontrolled crystallization that ruins a polymorph study before it starts.

Dri-Pure anti-bumping technology works alongside advanced temperature control to keep the evaporation process gentle and predictable, protecting the sample itself rather than just monitoring the process. eXalt technology takes the opposite approach for crystallization work, using controlled evaporation deliberately to produce usable crystals for polymorph screening and related studies, rather than treating crystallization as something to avoid.

longForm.heroHook: 6 or 12 positions, 4.5 liters of capacity. Built to clear the bottleneck, not join it.
heroParagraphs: Parallel evaporation bottlenecks usually happen because the evaporator itself becomes the slow step. HT Series 3i is built specifically to not be that.

Choose HT-6 or HT-12 for the throughput you actually need, with up to 4.5 liters of solvent capacity in one run. An integrated condenser keeps the whole system's footprint down, saving fume hood space a separate condenser would cost you.

A high-performance dry vacuum pump and F-Gas compliant, low-GWP refrigerant system keep the environmental footprint down too. SampleGuard temperature control protects against over-heating throughout the run.
longForm.statsIntro: The quick stats of the Genevac HT Series 3i Centrifugal Evaporator cover its throughput, capacity, and environmental performance.
